title: A nonempty regular open descends along a dominant finite type map of domains
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (an integral domain here means a nonzero commutative ring in which a product is zero only if one factor is zero) and let $R\to S$ be an injective ring homomorphism of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], with $S$ an integral domain. Suppose that $\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] contains a nonempty open subset $V$ such that $S_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] for every $\mathfrak q\in V$. Then $\operatorname{Spec}R$ contains a nonempty open subset $U$ such that $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular local for every $\mathfrak p\in U$.

source.place: Tag 07PA, lemma-J-0-goes-down; J-0 expanded using Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: Choose $\mathfrak q_0\in V$. By the basic-open basis lemma choose $g\in S$ with $\mathfrak q_0\in D(g)\subseteq V$; in particular $g\ne0$. Put $B=S_g=S[1/g]$. This is an $R$-algebra of finite type: if $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ generate $S$ over $R$, their images together with $g^{-1}$ generate $B$, since every fraction is $s/g^m$. It is a nonzero domain and $R\to B$ is injective: the zero-fraction criterion says that an element killed in $B$ is killed in $S$ by a power of $g$, which is nonzero in the domain $S$. Thus a nonzero $r\in R$ cannot be killed.

source.place: Tag 07PA, first sentence of proof: choose the regular principal open; Tags 00E0 and 00E4 for the basis and localization correspondence.

proof.text:
The finite-type Noetherian permanence lemma applied to $R	o B$ makes $B$ Noetherian. For any prime $P$ of $B$, the basic-open correspondence gives its contraction $\mathfrak q\in D(g)\subseteq V$. The localizations $B_P$ and $S_{\mathfrak q}$ are canonically isomorphic: $(s/g^m)/(t/g^n)$ maps to $sg^n/(tg^m)$, and the inverse sends $s/t$ to $(s/1)/(t/1)$. The denominators are legitimate because $g
otin\mathfrak q$ and $t/g^n
otin P$ precisely when $t
otin\mathfrak q$; cross multiplication and the zero-fraction relations make the two maps well-defined and inverse. By the hypothesis on $V$, every $B_P$ is regular local. Consequently $B$ is a regular ring by definition. Regular-local status is invariant under this isomorphism: it identifies the maximal ideals and their generating families, all ideals for Noetherianity, and prime chains for Krull dimension.

source.place: Tag 07PA, first sentence of proof; Tag 00FN for Noetherianity; Tag 00OD for the regular-ring condition.

proof.text: Apply Noetherian generic freeness to the original base $R$, the finite-type $R$-algebra $B$, and the $B$-module $M=B$, which is generated by $1$. All hypotheses hold: $R$ is the given Noetherian domain and step 1 proved finite type. It gives $0\ne a\in R$ such that $T=B_a$ is free over $A=R_a$. The localized module $(M)_a$ here is exactly the underlying $A$-module of $T$: both have fractions $b/a^j$ with the same equality criterion and scalar multiplication. No finiteness of the free basis over $A$ is asserted or needed. In Lean, IsLocalizedModule.iso identifies the localized module with the ring T as an R-module; LinearEquiv.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization upgrades it to an A-linear equivalence, transporting the free-module instance.

source.place: Tag 07PA, second sentence of proof; Tag 051R, algebra-lemma-generic-flatness-Noetherian, with M=B.

proof.text: For each prime P of T=B_a, the localization-of-localization isomorphism identifies T_P with the localization of B at its contracted prime. Since B is regular, every such local ring is regular local, and T is Noetherian as a localization of B. Thus T is regular. The image of a in B is nonzero by the injectivity from step 1; localization of the domain B away from this image is a nonzero domain. Consequently the free A-module T from step 3 is nontrivial. Its basis index set is nonempty, which is the hypothesis needed for faithful flatness of a free module.

source.place: Tag 07PA, second sentence of proof: regularity after the base localization and nonzero free rank.

proof.text: Here is the elementary basis calculation giving faithful flatness, rather than inferring it from freeness without checking rank. For any $A$-module $N$ define $T\otimes_A N\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{i\in I}N$ by $t\otimes n\longmapsto(c_i(t)n)_i$, where $c_i(t)$ are the finitely supported basis coordinates of $t$. Its inverse sends a finitely supported family $(n_i)_i$ to $\sum_i e_i\otimes n_i$. The tensor universal property, bilinearity, and $t=\sum_i c_i(t)e_i$ check both composites on pure tensors and basis-coordinate families; the maps commute with every map of $N$. Thus tensoring any complex with $T$ is the direct sum of its coordinate copies. A direct sum of an exact complex is exact: lift each of the finitely many nonzero coordinates of a kernel element. Conversely, if that direct-sum complex is exact, fix $i_0\in I$, insert a kernel element in coordinate $i_0$, lift in the direct sum, and project back to $i_0$ to find its preimage. Hence the complex is exact if and only if its tensor with $T$ is exact, which is precisely faithful flatness of $A\to T$. This argument covers infinite $I$ as well as finite nonzero rank. In Lean, use Mathlib's instance Module.FaithfullyFlat for a nontrivial free module; this already implements the nonempty-basis argument, so no new helper theorem is needed.

source.place: Tag 07PA, second sentence, expanding why the generic-free localization is faithfully flat; Tag 00HB, definition-flat (2),(4).

proof.text: Apply regular-ring faithfully flat descent to $A\to T$. Step 5 supplies faithful flatness and step 4 supplies regularity of $T$, including its Noetherianity. Its conclusion is that $A=R_a$ is a regular ring. This uses the descent theorem with exactly its stated hypotheses, without assuming that $R$ was already regular.

source.place: Tag 07PA, last sentence of proof, invoking Tag 07NG, lemma-descent-regular.

proof.text: Let $U=D(a)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$. It is open by the basic-open lemma and nonempty because the prime $(0)$ of the nonzero domain $R$ avoids $a\ne0$. For every $\mathfrak p\in U$ the same lemma supplies the corresponding prime $P$ of $A=R_a$. As in step 2, $(R_a)_P\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$ by $(r/a^m)/(s/a^n)\mapsto ra^n/(sa^m)$ with inverse $r/s\mapsto(r/1)/(s/1)$. The nonvanishing of the denominators modulo $\mathfrak p$ and the fraction relations verify these formulas. Since $A$ is regular by step 6, its prime localization at $P$, and therefore $R_{\mathfrak p}$, is regular local. This is the required nonempty regular open in $\operatorname{Spec}R$.

source.place: Tag 07PA, conclusion after shrinking the base; Tag 07P7, definition-J (1), expanded as the open D(a).
